counterargs.read: The rates market is doing the tightening: a front-end-led, real-rate-driven selloff with MOVE back above 90 and yen weakness, while funding, index credit and equity vol stay calm. That reads as duration repricing rather than Treasury intermediation stress -- dealers absorbed little of the 10Y. The risk is that higher real yields keep pressing high-beta (NVDA, consumer credit) and push USDJPY into the 162 BOJ zone. Confirmation of something worse would need HY OAS > 3.5%, SOFR-IORB > 8bp, or a weak 30Y on Nov 12.

transmission.bottom_line: Liquidity plumbing and Treasury auctions remain supportive (SOFR-IORB +2bp, bank demand +$21.6B, 20Y and 5Y TIPS cleared well). The new pressures are inflation and credit: oil crossed the 3% daily threshold ($103.27, +3.8%) with breakevens rising, and HY OAS widened 13bp to 3.40%, 10bp from the 3.5% line.
